newsitem.title: GERMANY: Juncker wants EU strategy vs market turmoil - paper.
newsitem.headline: Juncker wants EU strategy vs market turmoil - paper.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker called on Tuesday for a common European Union strategy to counter possible turbulence in financial markets in the six months before participants in the planned single currency are chosen.

Juncker, whose country took over the rotating EU presidency on Tuesday, said in a newspaper interview that the starting line-up of nations qualifying for the euro would become apparent in late October to early November at the latest.
That was when the first reliable estimates for 1997 economic growth and budget deficits would become available.
Markets would then "informally acknowledge who will definitely not join," Juncker, who is also Luxembourg's finance minister, was quoted as telling Germany's Boersen Zeitung.
As a result an "area of tension" should be expected, Juncker said, adding the EU would have to prepare for this. "We must not let ourselves be taken by surprise by the financial markets."

He declined to specify what measures were available to counter possible market turbulence ahead of decisions due in spring 1988 on which countries will be founder members of the single currency, the newspaper said.

Juncker said the conversion rates between the currencies of those nations qualifying for the euro should be fixed as soon as possible. "The parities will have to be fixed at the latest when the final choice has been made."

Juncker said a postponement of monetary union, scheduled to start on January 1, 1999, was legally possible under the Maastricht Treaty as long as it was decided before the end of 1997, but a delay was a "totally absurd scenario" that would have serious negative consequences.
In choosing EMU members, their prospects for long-term stability were as important as the "snapshot" of their adherence to the convergence criteria in 1997, Juncker said.
